title: Shadowing session: Customer cost + rollout workflows - notes and quick fixes
content:
Context
---
What: 90-minute remote shadowing of a single customer admin (MidMarket AI SaaS) using Redwood Console to configure a rollout to Dedicated capacity, tune batching/quantization, and inspect token-cost anomalies. Session run as part of our usability checks for the rollout + cost experience. Moderators: Avery (note taker), Ravi (product lead), Sofia (PM). Date: 2026-05-10. Customer contact: Elena Ruiz (Senior Platform Eng).

Participants & environment
- Customer: MidMarket AI SaaS, Redwood Dedicated customer on eu-west region.
- Persona: Platform engineer responsible for cost SLOs and rollout safety (canary/auto-fallback).
- Environment: shared sandbox with traffic replay, customer used Chrome 114 on MacOS.

Tasks observed (core flows)
1) Create new rollout: pick model variant, set canary percent, set duration, attach fallback variant
2) Configure batching and target latency objective on Dedicated pool
3) Inspect per-route token cost spike for last 24h and drill into suspected prompt causing high tokens
4) Initiate rollback after canary breach and confirm fallback routing activated

High-level takeaways
- Customer completed all tasks but needed repeated clicks and context switching; most friction at stage transitions (create -> review -> apply).
- Cost drill-down is valuable but the nav and filters are confusing (time range + model variant + route overlap).
- Rollout preview (simulation) was expected but missing; customer repeatedly asked "what happens before I apply?"
- Language used in labels ("fallback variant" vs "emergency fallback") caused hesitation about severity and expected behavior.
- Customer wanted an auditable, copyable JSON of the rollout spec to check into infra-as-code.

Direct quotes (verbatim where possible)
- "I don't want to click into three different panels to know if my canary will actually only hit 5% traffic."
- "Is fallback immediate or gradual? The label doesn't tell me if traffic will switch or if requests will queue."
- "Show me the cost delta estimate before I push. I need to justify this to finance."

Observed friction points (ranked)
1) Lack of a single-review surface: after building a rollout the review screen scattered key knobs across three columns. Severity: high; Frequency: every participant. Suggested fix: consolidated summary card + inline edit.
2) Cost filters ambiguous: time range + aggregation granularity unclear, model variant filter resets when switching routes. Severity: medium-high. Suggested fix: persist variant filter, add small help text describing aggregation window.
3) No rollout dry-run / simulation: participants expected synthetic traffic preview or traffic split visualization before apply. Severity: medium. Suggested fix: lightweight simulation modal showing projected traffic distribution and cost delta (estimate).
4) Terminology ambiguity: "fallback" vs "secondary" vs "graceful degrade". Severity: medium. Suggested fix: standardize to "emergency fallback (immediate)" and "graceful fallback (gradual)" with icons and tooltips.
5) Missing export-as-code: many customers want IaC artifacts. Severity: low-medium. Suggested fix: add "Export JSON / Terraform" button on rollout summary.

Wireframe / UI tweaks (quick sketches in words)
- Rollout composer: introduce 3-step left-to-right flow (Configure -> Review & Simulate -> Apply) with a top breadcrumb and a persistent summary card on the right showing canary %, traffic targets, cost delta estimate, and a single "Export" icon.
- Simulation modal: allow 30s synthetic preview showing split by route and model variant; show estimated tokens/day and $/day delta. Toggle between conservative/median/risky estimate.
- Cost explorer: add persistent variant pill filters and an aggregation selector (per-hour, 6h, 24h) with a help icon linking to a KB article.
- Label updates: append shortness indicator to fallback labels with hover text: "Immediate: route traffic is re-routed instantly" / "Gradual: traffic moves over X minutes".

Backlog items & priority (recommended)
- PRO-9876: Rollout composer summary card + Export JSON (Priority: P0-P1; effort: 5 dev wks)
- UX-204: Simulation modal prototype + backend estimate stub (Priority: P1; effort: 3 dev wks + 1 research)
- CORE-1234: Cost filter persistence + aggregation selector (Priority: P1; effort: 2 dev wks)
- DOC-431: KB article: "Understanding Rollout Fallbacks" + label glossary (Priority: P2; effort: 3 writer days)

Quick wins (can be shipped in 1 sprint)
- Persist model-variant filter across cost explorer navigation (1 dev + 1 QA, ~3–5 days).
- Small copy change: change "Fallback" to "Immediate fallback" where action is immediate and add tooltip (1 writer + 1 front-end change, ~2 days).
- Add "Export JSON" button that downloads current summary card spec (front-end only, stubbed backend, ~3 days).

Edge cases / risks noted during session
- Customers may have automation that expects the old semantics of fallback; renaming must preserve API compatibility. Recommend keep backend flag unchanged, only UI copy.
- Cost estimates rely on historical token rates; for variable prompt mixing this could under/over estimate—add confidence band.

Accessibility notes
- Review screen has several tiny checkboxes and pill filters that did not meet contrast targets in the session (checked with participant's high-contrast theme). Add audits for contrast and keyboard flow on the composer modal.

Next steps (owners & timing)
- Product: prioritize PRO-9876 and UX-204 for next planning cycle (owner: Sofia; due: 2026-06-01).
- Design: produce 2 variants of the consolidated summary card + simulation modal comps (owner: Jamie; due: 2026-05-20).
- Eng: spike backend estimate API to support conservative/median/risky scenarios (owner: Ravi; due: 2026-05-28).
- Docs: draft KB article and label glossary (owner: Maria Gonzalez; due: 2026-05-25).

Appendix: raw timestamps & short transcript snippets
00:03:12 - "Where's the cost delta?"
00:20:44 - "I need to show this JSON to the rest of my team"
00:52:10 - "If canary breaches, will it flip traffic immediately?"

Session artifacts
- Screen recording (internal drive): /recordings/shadowing-2026-05-10-elena.mp4 (internal link)
- Low-fi wireframe images attached to PR: Github PR 412 contains simple PSD/PNG comps.

Research notes (methodology reflections)
- Remote shadowing revealed how much customers rely on preview affordances; lab-based unmoderated tests had not surfaced this. Recommend adding 2 more shadowing sessions focused on rollback semantics for enterprise customers.

Concluding comment
Customers want confidence before they apply rollouts: consolidate key controls, show a lightweight simulation, and give a simple export path for infra review. Shipping the summary card + export and a basic simulation should notably reduce hesitation and support adoption of canary workflows on Dedicated.
